'''''Persicaria longiseta''''' is a species of flowering plant in the [[Polygonaceae|knotweed family]] known by the common names '''Oriental lady's thumb''', '''bristly lady's thumb''', '''Asiatic smartweed''', '''long-bristled smartweed''', '''low smartweed''', '''Asiatic waterpepper''', '''bristled knotweed''', '''bunchy knotweed''', and '''tufted knotweed'''. It is native to [[Asia]] (China, India, Russia, Japan, Malaysia, etc.),<ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=242339605 Flora of China, ''Polygonum longisetum'' Bruijn in Miquel, 1854.  <big>长鬃蓼</big> chang zong liao ]</ref> and it is present in North America and Europe as an [[introduced species]] and often a [[weed]].<ref name=feis>{{cite web |last=Stone |first=Katharine R. |year=2010 |url=https://www.fs.fed.us/database/feis/plants/forb/perlon/all.html |title=Persicaria longiseta |website=Fire Effects Information System, U.S. Department of Agriculture, Forest Service, Rocky Mountain Research Station, Fire Sciences Laboratory |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170528212846/https://www.fs.fed.us/database/feis/plants/forb/perlon/all.html |archive-date=2017-05-28}}</ref><ref>[http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/index1.php?scientific-name=persicaria+longiseta Altervista Flora Italiana, ''Persicaria longiseta'' (Bruijn) Kitag.]</ref>

''Persicaria longiseta'' is an annual herb with stems 30 to 80 centimeters (12–32 inches) long,<ref name=fna>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=242100101 Flora of North America. ''Persicaria longiseta''.] Flora of North America.</ref> sometimes reaching one meter (40 inches).<ref name=feis/> The hairless, branching stems may root at lower nodes that come in contact with the substrate. The leaves are lance-shaped and up to 8 centimeters (3.2 inches) long by 3 cm (1.2 inches) wide. They have bristly [[ochrea]]. The [[inflorescence]] is an elongate cluster up to 8 centimeters (3.2 inches) long and contains many pink flowers. The fruit is a small, smooth [[achene]].<ref name=fna/>

In its native region this plant is a common weed of [[paddy field|rice paddies]]. It was introduced to North America near [[Philadelphia, Pennsylvania|Philadelphia]] around 1910 and probably spread via the [[railroad]]s. It is present in much of the eastern United States and much of Canada.<ref>[http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Persicaria%20longiseta.png Biota of North America Program 2014 county distribution map]</ref> It grows in moist habitat types such as [[wetland]]s, as well as dry and upland habitat. It can be found in meadows, [[marsh]]es, [[mudflat]]s, riverbanks, [[floodplain]]s, [[levee]]s, and lowland and upland forests. It is [[invasive species|invasive]] in some areas.<ref name=feis/>
